title: Deficiency Balance Accounts: Length of the Last Broken Arrangement and the Restart Percent
content:
**Rule.** On an account held under Deficiency Balance Accounts the restart percent (the percentage of the balance at which a restart down payment is figured) reflects how long the latest broken arrangement ran. The restart run is the number of whole months from the latest broken arrangement's acceptance date to its broken date. A restart run of 9 whole months or more lowers the restart percent by 2.0 points, one of at least 4 but fewer than 9 whole months lowers it by 1.0 point, and a shorter restart run lowers it by no points. Whole months are counted as the difference in calendar months between the two dates, less one when the later date's day of the month is below the earlier date's.

The latest broken arrangement is the account's arrangement offer with the status broken whose broken date is the latest (plan or settlement alike); no two arrangements of an account break on the same day. The acceptance date is the date on which the borrower's acceptance of that offer is recorded.

## Ladder

| Restart run | Restart percent lowered by |
|---|---|
| 9 whole months or more | 2.0 points |
| 4 to 8 whole months | 1.0 point |
| 0 to 3 whole months | No points |

## Boundary pairs (hypothetical dates)

| Accepted on | Broken on | Whole months | Lowered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 January | 14 October of the same year | 8 | 1.0 point |
| 15 January | 15 October of the same year | 9 | 2.0 points |
| 15 January | 14 May of the same year | 3 | No points |
| 15 January | 15 May of the same year | 4 | 1.0 point |

## Basis Q&A

**The account has two broken arrangements.** Only the one with the latest broken date is measured.

**Does the time since the break matter here?** No; the run is measured from that arrangement's acceptance to its break.
